rejected.title: The multi-store model
card: Atkinson and Shiffrin's multi-store model says memory has three stores: sensory memory, short-term memory and long-term memory. Information moves forward through them in order, and retrieval brings it back from long-term memory into short-term memory when it is needed.
Sensory memory
holds raw input from the senses. It has a large capacity but lasts only a fraction of a second to a few seconds. Only what gets attention moves on.
Short-term memory
holds a small amount of information, about 5 to 9 items, for up to about 30 seconds. Rehearsal, such as repeating something in your head, keeps it there longer and can move it on.
Long-term memory
has an unlimited capacity and can hold information for years or a lifetime. Information is moved here by rehearsal.
rejected.remember: Attention moves information into short-term memory, rehearsal moves it into long-term memory, and retrieval brings it back.

a.q: A store holds only a handful of items, and they fade within half a minute unless rehearsed. Which store is it?
opts: Short-term memory
Sensory memory
Long-term memory
Rehearsal memory
a.why: Short-term memory has a small capacity and a short duration, and rehearsal keeps information there longer. Sensory memory is tempting, but it has a large capacity and lasts only a few seconds at most.
a.clue: Think of the store that sits in the middle of the model.

b.q: Priya hears a phone number once and repeats it aloud many times while she looks for a pen. What is repeating it most likely to do?
opts: Keep it in short-term memory and help move it on
Give it a larger capacity in sensory memory
Make it last for years in sensory memory
Remove it from short-term memory straight away
b.why: Rehearsal keeps information in short-term memory for longer and can move it into long-term memory. Sensory memory lasts only a few seconds, so rehearsal does not extend it.
b.clue: Which store does rehearsal help information leave?

problems.detail: 'Information moves between them in order' suggests a one-way flow. The Atkinson-Shiffrin model also has retrieval, where information moves from long-term memory back into short-term memory. Adding this would stop students thinking flow is only forwards.
